I thought this was an interesting take because I think it’s true.

Hold my beer.

The real goal for crypto is for companies and people to use it without feeling like they’re using crypto.

That’s what projects like @alignedlayer and @stripe are building toward.

Aligned makes blockchain verification happen in the background, while Stripe lets businesses use stablecoins without turning every customer into a crypto user.

Some Stripe users say around 20% of payment volume has moved to stablecoins, with costs roughly cut in half.

The same shift is happening in finance too.
Tokenized cash and Treasuries can move 24/7, and the on-chain RWA market is already around $38B.

Not every company will launch a token, but more and more will have crypto quietly running in the background.

tweets.text:
I expected Maple or Centrifuge to lead tokenized credit.

Neither does.

Here are the largest platforms by distributed tokenized credit value on @RWA_xyz:

1. @stokr_io: $1.40B
2. @maplefinance: $954.8M
3. @centrifuge: $747.4M
4. @HastraFi: $575.9M
5. Realiz: $500.0M
6. @Securitize: $475.3M
7. @chainlink CCIP: $371.9M
8. @onrefinance: $260.5M
9. @humafinance: $221.0M
10. @paretocredit: $219.0M

STOKR’s lead is mainly driven by two large Bitcoin-mining credit products that account for ~97% of its distributed value.

But the broader leaderboard is more interesting IMO. Tokenized credit is already spreading across everything from asset-backed lending and structured credit to reinsurance and PayFi.

It’s becoming a broader category than just putting private loans onchain.

#uranium #copper #silver #gold

⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE — AUGUST 23, 2026 ⚡

The macro setup for hard assets keeps getting stronger.

U.S. debt has crossed $40T, long-term bond yields are surging, oil is feeding renewed inflation fears and the Treasury’s expanded bond buybacks have revived the debasement trade. Capital is already responding: gold and precious-metals funds attracted another $2B+ last week.

☢️ URANIUM — Perhaps the most compelling setup of all. Spot is approaching $90/lb while the long-term price is near cycle highs — before replacement-rate contracting has really begun. Utilities are heading for a 14th consecutive year of contracting below reactor requirements. That buying eventually has to happen.

Meanwhile, $KAP’s new sulphuric-acid plant has been delayed, keeping attention firmly on the acid availability and cost pressures facing the world’s largest uranium producer.

Record/near-record term pricing before the real contracting cycle starts. Think about that.

🟠 COPPER — Last week’s extraordinary LME squeeze showed just how tight available metal can become, with cash copper briefly commanding a $500+/t premium. Inventories have since rebounded as metal rushed into warehouses, easing the immediate squeeze — but Chile now expects copper production to fall in 2026.

Against accelerating AI, grid and electrification demand, the structural supply problem hasn’t disappeared.

🥈 SILVER — The story just became more bullish.

India’s import collapse increasingly looks like a temporary regulatory disruption rather than demand destruction. Banks and traders are securing licences and imports are beginning to pick up again.

At the same time, renewed inflation, debt and currency-debasement fears are pulling investors toward precious metals. Add six consecutive years of silver deficits, weak growth in mine supply and silver’s dependence on byproduct production from copper/base-metal mines.

If Indian buying normalizes while Western investment demand accelerates, silver could face a very different demand picture than just a few months ago.

🥇 GOLD — The monetary trade is back.

Gold is benefiting from the uncomfortable combination of huge government debt + rising inflation risk + questions over fiat currencies and sovereign bonds. Treasury buybacks added fuel last week, while precious-metals funds continue attracting capital.

Ray Dalio is again urging investors to own substantial gold exposure as protection against debt and monetary-system risks.

👀 NEXT WEEK: PCE inflation, U.S. GDP and Jackson Hole put the Fed, yields and dollar back at center stage.

Higher inflation strengthens the hard-asset argument. A dovish Fed weakens the dollar.

Either scenario could keep capital rotating toward scarce real assets.

And uranium, copper, silver and gold sit right at the center of that trade.

👇 Want to know which companies I’m watching most closely across these themes? See my updated top picks below.

Against accelerating AI, grid and electrification demand, the structural supply problem hasn’t disappeared.

India’s import collapse increasingly looks like a temporary regulatory disruption rather than demand destruction. Banks and traders are securing licences and imports are beginning to pick up again.

At the same time, renewed inflation, debt and currency-debasement fears are pulling investors toward precious metals. Add six consecutive years of silver deficits, weak growth in mine supply and silver’s dependence on byproduct production from copper/base-metal mines.

🥇 GOLD — The monetary trade is back.

Gold is benefiting from the uncomfortable combination of huge government debt + rising inflation risk + questions over fiat currencies and sovereign bonds. Treasury buybacks added fuel last week, while precious-metals funds continue attracting capital.

Ray Dalio is again urging investors to own substantial gold exposure as protection against debt and monetary-system risks.

Either scenario could keep capital rotating toward scarce real assets.

And uranium, copper, silver and gold sit right at the center of that trade.

Producers & Developers

Explorers

$SYH – One of my preferred Athabasca prospect generators, with 44 projects and multiple partner-funded exploration programs.

$M.CN – All four initial Lucky Cliff holes hit broad near-surface uranium mineralization, including 19.96 m at 269 ppm eU₃O₈. Myriad has also completed the Rush acquisition, consolidating 100% of Copper Mountain.

🥈 SILVER

Producers

$HL – Q2 silver production reached 4.2M oz, with Lucky Friday setting a quarterly production record.

$AG – Q2 revenue jumped 57%, free cash flow reached $194.6M and net earnings more than doubled YoY.

$PAAS – Strong Q2 with 6.47M oz silver, $344M attributable free cash flow and progress at La Colorada Skarn.

Explorers

$HYMC – Fresh drilling extended both high-grade systems, including 12.5 m at 375 g/t Ag at Vortex.

$GRSL.V – San Marcial continues delivering, including 21.9 m at 168 g/t Ag, with 6.15 m at 447 g/t.

$JTWO – My wildcard. Sierra Plata is advancing toward its maiden drill program, with geophysics refining the targets.

🟠 COPPER

$CGNT – My primary copper exposure and now up over 100% from my C$0.54 entry. Recently secured a C$31M strategic financing and 10-year Trafigura offtake agreement covering 20% of future Mocoa concentrate production.

💎 FLUORSPAR

$CTV.V – An interesting U.S. critical-minerals opportunity. CleanTech Vanadium is advancing its Kentucky fluorspar assets toward drilling and potential domestic production at a time when the U.S. remains heavily dependent on imported fluorspar.

⚫ GRAPHENE

$HG $HGRAF – Still my largest holding. HydroGraph is progressing its Texas scale-up, expanding institutional exposure and pursuing U.S. federal/defense opportunities while advancing commercial adoption of its high-purity graphene.

Disclosure: I have paid partnerships with Myriad Uranium, Skyharbour Resources and CleanTech Vanadium.

Common Sense Is Not So Common Among Algos

$URGN is now up 5x since the tweet below, from roughly $10 to $50. It reached our price target, and we decided to close 90% of the position.

But the lesson here is much bigger than $URGN.

The new market is dominated by algos. They see a bad print, they sell. They don’t ask questions. They don’t look for logic. If expectations were X and the number comes in at X minus one, they immediately hit the sell button.

You saw it with $WGS a month ago when it fell to around $55 after earnings. Today it is around $86.

You saw it again with $ZIM last week, when the stock dropped about 7% on somewhat soft earnings from a quarter that didn’t really matter, and recovered most of that drop within a couple of days.

And then there is $URGN, which you can see below.

The headline looks bad, the stock gets sold first, and only afterward does the market actually stop and understand what happened.

This is why I think the real sweet spot is companies between roughly $500M and $5B market cap. Big enough to be real businesses, but small enough that analysts can still be inefficient and the market can completely misunderstand the story.

I urge you to read the entire $URGN tweet below, slowly. After a successful Phase 3, the stock was trading almost where it had been trading before the Phase 3 because of technicalities and misunderstanding. The market eventually corrected it, and the few who understood what was actually happening and followed the story closely had the opportunity to make bank.

A lot of people study how George Soros broke the Bank of England. Great story, but mostly entertainment for the average investor.

Study the $URGN case instead. That is something you can actually use to make money.

You saw it again with $ZIM last week, when the stock dropped about 7% on somewhat soft earnings from a quarter that didn’t really matter, and recovered most of that drop within a couple of days.

And then there is $URGN, which you can see below.

The headline looks bad, the stock gets sold first, and only afterward does the market actually stop and understand what happened.

This is why I think the real sweet spot is companies between roughly $500M and $5B market cap. Big enough to be real businesses, but small enough that analysts can still be inefficient and the market can completely misunderstand the story.

I urge you to read the entire $URGN tweet below, slowly. After a successful Phase 3, the stock was trading almost where it had been trading before the Phase 3 because of technicalities and misunderstanding. The market eventually corrected it, and the few who understood what was actually happening and followed the story closely had the opportunity to make bank.

A lot of people study how George Soros broke the Bank of England. Great story, but mostly entertainment for the average investor.

Study the $URGN case instead. That is something you can actually use to make money.

Integrity comes from the Latin word integritas, meaning "one" or "whole." People who are one way on the inside and another way on the outside--i.e., not "whole"--lack integrity; they have "duality" instead. While presenting your view as something other than it is can sometimes be easier in the moment (because you can avoid conflict, or embarrassment, or achieve some other short-term goal), the second and third-order effects of having integrity and avoiding duality are immense. 

People who are one way on the inside and another on the outside become conflicted and often lose touch with their own values. It's difficult for them to be happy and almost impossible for them to be their best. #principleoftheday
